brief: The S&P 500 remains in an uptrend but has consolidated since its early-August breakout, holding above the breakout level and its 50-day moving average. Breadth has cooled: only 28% of constituents trade above their 20-day moving average, and the equal-weight index's relative performance broke below its uptrend line as mega-cap Technology tries to reassert leadership. Longer-term participation stays constructive at 63% above the 200-day average, with Energy and Financials showing the strongest breadth (over 80% above the 200-day average) versus Consumer Discretionary and Utilities (under 40%). This week's PPI and CPI are the last data before next week's Fed meeting. Markets are pricing a 63% probability of a September rate hike: a softer print could buy the Fed time, a hotter one would reinforce the hawkish outlook. The 10-year yield sits at its highest level since 2023, driven by expanding term premium rather than inflation expectations, pressuring valuations, though contained credit spreads and sub-2.5% breakeven inflation expectations argue against economic stress. Elevated oil on geopolitical tensions is a growth headwind but supports Energy sector leadership. Raymond James views any meaningful pullback as a buying opportunity.
